title: Introductions & First Impressions
lead: Six cards, sixty minutes, ten words. Everyone speaks from the first minute, and every card carries a sentence frame you can read off the table.
warmup: Point to your name on your phone. Say it to your partner.
say: My name is Ana. / Nice to meet you.
words: A word you say when you meet someone.
A person you like and know well.
A land with its own flag.
A big town with many people.
The work you do for money.
My job is in a shop.
This is a photo of my family.
question: Is your city friendly? Why?
model: For me, my city is friendly because people say hello.
choices: a big city or a small town
talk to new people or stay with friends
a morning person or an evening person
pref_example: I prefer a small town because it is quiet.

roleplay.title: meet someone new
roleplay.scenario: Student A is new at the club, Student B is a member. Say your name and ask two questions.

future.chunks: Tomorrow, I will… / Next week, I want to…
future.prompts: Who will you meet tomorrow? What do you want to do next week?
future.model: Next week I want to meet a new friend.

takeaway: Say your name + one word you liked today.
weaker: let Card 4 be read word for word from the card.
stronger: add a third question — "Do you live near here?"

title: Work & Career Choices
lead: Ten work words, one opinion question, and a small conversation at a shop counter. No grammar lecture — just frames people can use on Monday.
warmup: Show your phone. Is your job in the phone? Point to one work app.
say: I work in a shop. / I start at nine.
words: The work you do for money.
My job is in a shop.
A room where people work at desks.
A machine for work and email.
A message you send from a computer.
I write ten emails a day.
question: Is your job good for you? Why?
model: For me, my job is good because the people are nice.
choices: an office job or a job at home
a morning shift or an evening shift
a big company or a small company
pref_example: I prefer a morning shift because I sleep early.

roleplay.title: ask about a job
roleplay.scenario: Student A has a small shop. Student B wants a job there. Ask about the hours and the money.

future.chunks: Next year, I want to… / Tomorrow, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to do next year? What will you do after work tomorrow?
future.model: Next year I want to work in a bigger office.

takeaway: One word from today + one job you want.
weaker: use only three questions in Card 4 and write them on the board.
stronger: the shop says no, so B asks about a different job — "Do you know a shop with a job?"

title: Time Management & Daily Priorities
lead: Time words are the easiest words to use at A0: today, tomorrow, nine o'clock. This session turns them into appointments and plans.
warmup: Look at your phone. What time is it now? Say the time to your partner.
say: It is nine o'clock. / I am busy today.
words: A thing that shows the time.
The clock is on the wall.
The place or the thing you do for money.
I go to work at eight.
To rest with your eyes closed.
What you will do and when.
question: Are you busy every day? Why?
model: For me, I am busy every day because I work and cook.
choices: a busy day or a free day
work in the morning or work in the evening
make a plan or no plan
pref_example: I prefer a free day because I can sleep.

roleplay.title: make an appointment
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at a reception desk. Student B wants an appointment this week.

future.chunks: Tonight, I will… / Tomorrow, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you do tonight? What do you want to do tomorrow morning?
future.model: Tonight I will sleep early.

takeaway: One word + one time you will do something tomorrow.
weaker: put three times on the board (nine, twelve, three) and let B point.
stronger: Monday is full, so the receptionist offers Tuesday at four — B must accept or ask for another day.

title: Family Roles & Responsibilities
lead: Family words are personal, so this session runs on photos and short answers. Card 4 is a friendly conversation, not a debate.
warmup: Show a photo on your phone. Who is in the photo? Say one word.
say: This is my sister. / She lives in my city.
words: The woman in your family with children.
The man in your family with children.
A girl or woman with the same parents.
A boy or man with the same parents.
To make food hot and ready.
To make a place not dirty.
To do part of the work for someone.
To go to someone's home for a time.
We visit my mother on Sunday.
question: Who cooks in your home?
model: For me, I cook, and my sister cleans.
choices: a big family or a small family
cook at home or eat out
live with family or live alone
pref_example: I prefer a small family because it is quiet.

roleplay.title: ask about a family
roleplay.scenario: Two friends talk about their families. Ask, answer, then swap.
frames: Do you have brothers or sisters?
No, she lives in another city.

future.chunks: This weekend, I will… / Next month, I want to…
future.prompts: Who will you visit this weekend? What do you want to do with your family next month?
future.model: This weekend I will visit my mother.

takeaway: One word + one person you will see this week.
weaker: write the six answers on the board so B can read them.
stronger: add a follow-up — "Who cooks in her home?" — so the answers get longer.

title: Appearance & First Judgments
lead: Describing people needs only two patterns: is and has. Ten words, three choices, and a short visit to an optician.
warmup: Look at your partner. Say one true sentence: "You have brown eyes."
say: She has long hair. / He is tall.
words: You wear them to see well.
question: Do you like your photo? Why?
model: For me, I don't like my photo because my eyes are closed.
choices: short hair or long hair
glasses or no glasses
formal clothes or comfortable clothes
pref_example: I prefer comfortable clothes because I walk a lot.

roleplay.title: at the optician
roleplay.scenario: Student A works in an optician's shop. Student B wants new glasses.

future.chunks: Next month, I want to… / Tomorrow, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to buy next month? What will you wear tomorrow?
future.model: Next month I want to buy new glasses.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will wear tomorrow.
weaker: let A point at the glasses and say only "These? These?" plus the price.
stronger: the glasses are too small, so B asks for a different pair and a different price.

title: Morning Routines & Productivity
lead: The morning is the easiest place to start speaking: everybody has one, and every action has a picture. Card 4 is breakfast at a café counter.
warmup: Mime one morning action. Your partner says the word.
say: I wake up at seven. / I drink coffee.
words: A sound that wakes you up.
I take a shower at seven.
The first meal of the day.
A big vehicle for many people.
I take the bus at eight.
To go fast because you are late.
I go to work at nine.
I am tired in the morning.
question: Is your morning good or bad? Why?
model: For me, my morning is good because I have time for coffee.
choices: early morning or late night
breakfast at home or breakfast at a café
walk to work or take the bus
pref_example: I prefer to walk because the bus is late.

roleplay.title: buy breakfast
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at a café. Student B wants breakfast before work.
frames: Thank you. Have a good day.

future.chunks: Tomorrow, I will… / Next week, I want to…
future.prompts: What time will you wake up tomorrow? What do you want to change in your morning?
future.model: Tomorrow I will wake up at six and walk to work.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will do tomorrow morning.
weaker: put the three prices on the board and let B point to the total.
stronger: the sandwich is finished, so B chooses something else and asks the price again.

title: Evening Wind-Down & Work-Life Balance
lead: After work is when adults actually have time to talk. This session keeps the language small so the conversation can be long.
warmup: Mime one thing you do after work. Your partner says it.
say: In the evening I watch TV. / I relax at home.
words: a dark sky with a lamp
The time after work, before night.
In the evening I am at home.
A screen for films and news.
I watch TV for one hour.
We take a walk after dinner.
To rest and do nothing hard.
I read a book in bed.
I go to bed at eleven.
question: What do you do in the evening? Is it good for you?
model: For me, my evening is good because I walk and then relax.
choices: watch TV or read a book
walk after dinner or sit on the sofa
phone in bed or no phone in bed
pref_example: I prefer a book because the TV is too loud.

roleplay.title: invite a friend for dinner
roleplay.scenario: Student A invites Student B for dinner. B says yes and asks what to bring.
frames: Do you want to come for dinner?
Just bread. See you at seven.

future.chunks: Tonight, I will… / Next week, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you do tonight? What do you want to do after work next week?
future.model: Tonight I will walk for twenty minutes and go to bed early.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will do tonight.
weaker: cut the invitation to three lines and let B read them.
stronger: B is busy tonight, so they have to find another day and time.

title: Home & Living Preferences
lead: Rooms and furniture give A0 speakers something to point at and name. Card 4 turns that into a phone call about a flat.
warmup: Point to three things in this room. Name them.
say: There is a kitchen. / My flat is small.
words: A home on one floor of a building.
My flat is on the third floor.
A home with its own door to the street.
They live in a big house.
A space with walls and a door.
Glass in the wall for light.
A person in the next home.
You open the door with them.
question: Do you like your home? Why?
model: For me, I like my home because it is quiet and near the bus.
choices: a flat or a house
in the city centre or outside the city
an old building or a new building
pref_example: I prefer an old building because the rooms are big.

roleplay.title: call about a flat
roleplay.scenario: Student A has a flat to rent. Student B calls and asks three questions.
frames: Hello. I want to see the flat.

future.chunks: Next year, I want to… / This weekend, I will…
future.prompts: Where do you want to live next year? What will you do at home this weekend?
future.model: Next year I want to live in a flat near the park.

takeaway: One word + one thing you want in your next home.
weaker: write the rent on a paper card so the numbers are read, not invented.
stronger: the flat has no lift and B lives on the fifth floor — B must ask about it.

title: Minimalism vs Comfort at Home
lead: "Minimalism" is a big word for a simple action: keep it or give it away. That action is Card 4.
warmup: Look in your bag. What do you keep and never use? Say one thing.
say: I keep this. / I don't need this.
words: A thing you put other things in.
A flat board for things on a wall.
The box for things you throw away.
The paper is in the bin.
question: Is your home full of things? Is that good?
model: For me, my home is full, and I think it is too much.
choices: many things or few things
keep old things or give them away
buy new things or use the old ones
pref_example: I prefer few things because I can clean fast.

roleplay.title: give things away
roleplay.scenario: Student A is moving to a smaller flat. Student B takes some things.
frames: Yes, thank you. What is it?
OK, I can give it to my sister.

future.chunks: This weekend, I will… / Next month, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you clean this weekend? What do you want to give away?
future.model: This weekend I will clean my shelf and give away three books.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will give away.
weaker: use only three objects on the table and let B point.
stronger: B wants the lamp but has no space, so they have to explain why not.

title: Food Culture & Personal Taste
lead: Food is the safest topic in any language: everyone has an opinion and a photo. This session uses both.
warmup: Open your phone. Find one food photo. Show it and say the word.
say: In my country we eat rice. / It is very good.
words: I buy bread in the morning.
Hot food you eat with a spoon.
To make food ready with heat.
To put food in your mouth to check it.
question: What food is good for you? Why?
model: For me, soup is good because it is hot and cheap.
choices: food from home or restaurant food
sweet food or salty food
cook at home or buy food
pref_example: I prefer home food because I know the salt.

roleplay.title: talk about food from your country
roleplay.scenario: Two people describe one dish from home. Ask, answer, then swap.

future.chunks: This weekend, I want to cook… / Tonight, I will eat…
future.prompts: What do you want to cook this weekend? What will you eat tonight?
future.model: This weekend I want to cook rice and fish.

takeaway: One food word + one dish you will eat this week.
weaker: give each student a food picture card and let them read the sentence from the card.
stronger: add a comparison — "Which is better, your food or my food?"

title: Restaurants & Social Eating
lead: Ordering food is the most useful A0 conversation there is. Card 4 runs it twice, so both people get to be the waiter.
warmup: Look at the menu on your table. Point to one food. What is it?
say: It is a menu. / This is water. / I like soup.
words: The list of food and drinks.
Can I see the menu, please?
The person who brings food to your table.
The furniture you sit at to eat.
To tell the waiter what you want.
The paper that shows how much you pay.
Extra money you leave for the waiter.
a happy face with a fork
question: Is a restaurant good for you? Why?
model: For me, a restaurant is good because the food is delicious.
choices: eat at home or eat in a restaurant
a quiet restaurant or a busy restaurant
pay by card or pay cash
pref_example: I prefer a quiet restaurant because I can talk.

roleplay.title: order a meal
roleplay.scenario: Student A is the waiter, Student B is the customer. Order one drink and one dish, then ask for the bill.
frames: Can I see the menu, please?
One water, please. Is it cold?

future.chunks: Tonight, I will… / Next weekend, I want to eat…
future.prompts: What will you eat tonight? Where do you want to eat next weekend?
future.model: Tonight I will cook pasta. Next weekend I want to eat in a new restaurant.

takeaway: One word from today + one place you want to eat next week.
weaker: use two choices in Card 3, and let Card 4 be read word for word.
stronger: the dish is finished, so the customer must choose again — "Do you have soup? No? OK, I want the salad."

title: Money Habits & Spending Priorities
lead: Prices are numbers you already know. This session puts them to work at a shop counter, with no grammar beyond "how much".
warmup: Take out a coin or a note. Say how much it is.
say: It is five euros. / I pay by card.
words: I save twenty euros a month.
I spend too much on coffee.
The place that keeps your money.
question: Is it easy to save money? Why?
model: For me, it is difficult because the city is expensive.
choices: pay by card or pay cash
save the money or spend it
buy the cheap one or buy the good one
pref_example: I prefer cash because I spend less.

roleplay.title: pay in a shop
roleplay.scenario: Student A works in a shop. Student B buys one thing and pays.
frames: Thank you. Have a good day.

future.chunks: Next month, I will… / This year, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you save for next month? What do you want to buy this year?
future.model: Next month I will save fifty euros for a new phone.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will not buy this month.
weaker: put three prices on the board and let B point to the one they want.
stronger: the card machine is broken, so B has to pay cash and check the change.

title: Fashion & Identity
lead: Clothes are vocabulary you wear. Card 4 is a changing room, which gives every student a reason to say "too big" and "too small".
warmup: Look at your partner's shoes. Say the colour.
say: I wear black shoes. / This is my size.
words: Clothes for the top of your body.
You wear them on your feet.
Clothes for a woman, top and skirt together.
How big or small clothes are.
To have clothes on your body.
I wear a jacket in winter.
question: Do clothes say something about a person? Why?
model: For me, clothes say a lot because I wear a uniform.
choices: new clothes or old clothes
bright colours or dark colours
comfortable clothes or beautiful clothes
pref_example: I prefer comfortable clothes because I walk to work.

roleplay.title: buy a jacket
roleplay.scenario: Student A works in a clothes shop. Student B wants a jacket in the right size.
frames: Do you want to try it on?
Yes, please. It is too small.

future.chunks: Next month, I want to buy… / Tomorrow, I will wear…
future.prompts: What do you want to buy next month? What will you wear tomorrow?
future.model: Next month I want to buy a warm jacket.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will wear tomorrow.
weaker: write the three sizes on cards and let B hand one to A.
stronger: the jacket is the last one and it is too expensive — B asks for something cheaper.

title: Weather & Lifestyle Choices
lead: Weather is the one topic every stranger shares. Ten words, three choices, and a short conversation about plans that depend on the sky.
warmup: Look out of the window. Say one word about the weather.
say: It is cold today. / I have an umbrella.
words: The light in the sky in the day.
White cold water from the sky.
I wear a coat in winter.
You hold it in the rain.
question: Do you like the weather today? Why?
model: For me, today is good because it is not too hot.
choices: hot weather or cold weather
summer or winter
walk in the rain or stay at home
pref_example: I prefer winter because I can wear my coat.

roleplay.title: make a plan about the weather
roleplay.scenario: Two friends want to go out today. Look out of the window and decide.

future.chunks: This weekend, if it is sunny, I will… / Next summer, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you do this weekend if it is sunny? Where do you want to go next summer?
future.model: This weekend, if it is sunny, I will walk in the park.

takeaway: One weather word + one plan for the weekend.
weaker: draw two weather symbols (sun, rain) and let students point.
stronger: the forecast says rain all weekend, so the pair has to change the plan twice.

title: Hobbies & Personal Growth
lead: Everyone has one thing they do for free. This session finds it, names it, and puts it in a sentence.
warmup: Mime your hobby. The group guesses the word.
say: My hobby is music. / I play the guitar.
words: I listen to music at night.
To move your body to music.
To look at words and understand them.
To make a picture with a pen.
I learn English at the club.
Time when you do not work.
In my free time I draw.
question: What do you do in your free time?
model: For me, I draw in my free time because it is quiet.
choices: music or sport
learn alone or learn in a class
a free hobby or a hobby you pay for
pref_example: I prefer a class because I meet people.

roleplay.title: ask about a class
roleplay.scenario: Student A teaches a small guitar class. Student B wants to join.
frames: We have a class on Tuesday.

future.chunks: Next year, I want to learn… / This weekend, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to learn next year? What will you do this weekend?
future.model: Next year I want to learn to swim.

takeaway: One word + one thing you want to learn.
weaker: give B the three questions written on a card to read aloud.
stronger: the Tuesday class is full, so A offers Thursday and B must choose.

title: Sports, Health & Competition
lead: Sport gives beginners verbs they can mime: run, swim, play, win. Card 4 is a conversation at a gym desk.
warmup: Mime one sport. Your partner says the word.
say: I play football. / I go swimming.
words: To move fast on your feet.
A game with a ball and two teams.
A place with machines for exercise.
The gym is near my home.
To be first in a game.
I am tired after the gym.
question: Do you like sport? Why?
model: For me, sport is good because I sleep better after it.
choices: play a sport or watch a sport
exercise alone or in a team
exercise in the morning or in the evening
pref_example: I prefer the evening because I am tired in the morning.

roleplay.title: join a gym
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at a gym. Student B wants to join.
frames: I want to join the gym.

future.chunks: Next week, I will… / This year, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you do for your body next week? What do you want to try this year?
future.model: Next week I will swim two times.

takeaway: One sport word + one thing you will do next week.
weaker: write three times (six, eight, ten) on the board for B to choose from.
stronger: the gym has a cheaper plan without a trainer — B must compare the two.

title: City Life vs Small Town
lead: Comparing two places is the first real opinion a beginner can defend. Card 4 adds a small map and a stranger.
warmup: Name one place near your home: a park, a shop, a café.
say: There is a park near my home.
words: A big town with many people.
A place smaller than a city.
I live in a small town.
a few houses and a tree
A green place in a city.
A place where you buy things.
There is a shop on my street.
To have your home in a place.
I live in a small town.
question: Is a city good for you? Why?
model: For me, the city is good because everything is near.
choices: a city or a small town
a park or a café
live near work or live far from work
pref_example: I prefer a small town because it is quiet.

roleplay.title: ask for directions
roleplay.scenario: Student B is new in the city. Student A lives here. B wants the park.
frames: Excuse me, where is the park?

future.chunks: Next year, I want to live… / This weekend, I will go to…
future.prompts: Where do you want to live next year? Where will you go this weekend?
future.model: Next year I want to live in a small town near the sea.

takeaway: One place word + one place you will go this weekend.
weaker: draw a simple map with three streets and let A point while speaking.
stronger: B asks for a second place (a pharmacy) and A must give a longer route.

title: Transport Choices & Sustainability
lead: Transport is the language of getting to work on time. Card 4 is a ticket office, and the clock is the complication.
warmup: Mime how you came here today. The group guesses: bus, bike, walk.
say: I come by bus. / The bus is late.
words: A big vehicle for many people.
I take the bus at eight.
A vehicle with two wheels and pedals.
I go to work by bike.
A car you pay to travel in.
The paper you buy to travel.
The place where a bus stops.
The stop is near my home.
question: How do you go to work? Is it good?
model: For me, the bike is good because it is cheap and fast.
choices: the bus or the bike
a taxi or a walk
a paper ticket or a ticket on your phone
pref_example: I prefer the train because the bus is always late.

roleplay.title: buy a ticket
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at the ticket office. Student B wants a ticket to the city centre.
frames: One ticket to the city centre, please.
Single, please. How much is it?
Platform three. It is ten minutes late.

future.chunks: Tomorrow, I will go by… / Next weekend, I want to go to…
future.prompts: How will you go to work tomorrow? Where do you want to go next weekend?
future.model: Tomorrow I will go by train, and next weekend I want to go to the lake.

takeaway: One transport word + one place you will go next week.
weaker: use three destinations with the prices written on the board.
stronger: the train is cancelled, so the clerk offers a bus and B must ask about the time again.

title: Job Satisfaction & Motivation
lead: Talking about work at A0 means talking about feelings and small requests, not careers. Card 4 is asking for a day off.
warmup: Say one good thing and one bad thing about your job. One word each.
say: My job is good. / The money is bad.
words: To do part of the work for someone.
I want to change my job.
A day when you do not work.
question: Are you happy at work? Why?
model: For me, I am happy at work because my team is friendly.
choices: a good team or good money
the same job or a new job
learn new things or do the same work
pref_example: I prefer a good team because the days are fast.

roleplay.title: ask for a day off
roleplay.scenario: Student B wants a day off. Student A is the boss and needs a reason.
frames: Can I have Friday off, please?

future.chunks: Next year, I want to… / Next month, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to change next year? What will you do in your next job?
future.model: Next year I want to change my job and start later.

takeaway: One word + one thing you want to change at work.
weaker: give the boss three possible answers on the board to choose from.
stronger: the boss says no, so B has to ask for a different day and give a better reason.

title: Emotions & Mental Wellbeing
lead: Feelings are A0 grammar with a big payoff: "I am tired" is a full conversation opener. Keep the session light and practical.
warmup: Show one face: happy, tired or worried. Your partner says the word.
say: I am tired today. / I feel good.
words: He is sad about his job.
I am angry with the bus.
I feel calm after a walk.
A person you like and know well.
question: What do you do when you are stressed?
model: For me, I walk when I am stressed because it helps.
choices: talk to a friend or stay alone
walk outside or sleep
music or silence
pref_example: I prefer to talk because my friend is a good listener.

roleplay.title: ask a friend how they are
roleplay.scenario: Two friends meet after work. B has a difficult week.

future.chunks: This weekend, I will… / Next week, I want to…
future.prompts: How will you relax this weekend? What do you want to do less next week?
future.model: This weekend I will walk and sleep, and next week I want to work less.

takeaway: One feeling word + one thing you will do to relax.
weaker: put six faces on the table and let students point instead of naming the feeling.
stronger: A has the same problem and they have to suggest two solutions to each other.

title: Health Choices & Prevention
lead: Health talk at A0 is a shopping list of small habits. Ten words, three choices, and a pharmacy conversation everyone will need eventually.
warmup: Point to your body: head, stomach, throat. Say the words with your partner.
say: I sleep eight hours. / I drink water every day.
words: Rest with your eyes closed at night.
I drink two litres of water.
I eat fruit in the morning.
Plants you cook or eat in salad.
I take a walk after lunch.
a person in a white coat
The person who helps sick people.
I go to the doctor on Monday.
What you take when you are sick.
To stop working for a time.
question: What is good for your health? Why?
model: For me, walking is good because it is free and easy.
choices: walk every day or go to the gym
cook at home or order food
sleep six hours or sleep eight hours
pref_example: I prefer to cook because restaurant food has too much salt.

roleplay.title: at the pharmacy
roleplay.scenario: Student A is the pharmacist. Student B has a headache.
frames: Good morning. Can I help you?
Take this, two times a day.

future.chunks: Next week, I will… / This month, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you do for your health next week? What do you want to change this month?
future.model: Next week I will walk thirty minutes every day.

takeaway: One word + one small health goal.
weaker: give the customer a card with the symptom written on it.
stronger: the pharmacy is out of the medicine, so A suggests a doctor and B books a time.

title: Time Perception & Punctuality
lead: Being late is a cultural topic you can handle with three words: sorry, bus, wait. Card 4 rehearses the apology until it feels normal.
warmup: Look at your phone. Say the time. Now say a time you are usually busy.
say: I am sorry I am late. / The bus was late.
words: a person at a bus stop
A thing that shows the time.
To go fast because you are late.
A word you say when you are late.
question: Are you usually early or late? Why?
model: For me, I am usually early because I don't like to hurry.
choices: arrive early or arrive on time
wait ten minutes or leave
use a clock or use your phone
pref_example: I prefer to arrive early because I can relax.

roleplay.title: you are late for a meeting
roleplay.scenario: Student B arrives late. Student A is waiting.

future.chunks: Tomorrow, I will leave… / Next week, I want to…
future.prompts: What time will you leave tomorrow? What do you want to change about your mornings?
future.model: Tomorrow I will leave at eight and arrive on time.

takeaway: One time word + one time you will arrive tomorrow.
weaker: let A accept the apology with one word ("OK") and keep the scene at four lines.
stronger: the meeting is important, so A is not happy and B has to explain and apologise twice.

title: Shopping Ethics & Consumer Choices
lead: "Ethics" becomes speakable at A0 when it turns into three questions: where is it from, who made it, and can I return it.
warmup: Look at one thing on your desk or in your bag. Where is it from?
say: It is from Spain. / I buy local food.
words: A place where you buy things.
A bag from a shop, bad for the sea.
The paper that shows what you paid.
To give something back to the shop.
To take one of two things.
question: Do you buy local food? Why?
model: For me, I buy local food because it is fresh.
choices: a local shop or a big supermarket
cheap things or good things
a new phone or the old phone
pref_example: I prefer the local shop because the people know me.

roleplay.title: ask where food is from
roleplay.scenario: Student A works in a small shop. Student B asks about the food and then returns something.
frames: No, sorry. The cheese is local.
I want to return this bag.

future.chunks: Next month, I want to buy… / This weekend, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to buy local next month? What will you do with old things at home?
future.model: Next month I want to buy local vegetables at the market.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will buy locally.
weaker: cut the return part and keep only the "where is this from" exchange.
stronger: B has no receipt, so A has to explain the shop rules politely.

title: Healthcare Access & Expectations
lead: The first real conversation many newcomers need is booking a doctor's appointment. Card 4 is exactly that phone call.
warmup: Point to the body words: head, stomach, throat, back. Say them with your partner.
say: I want an appointment. / I have a pain here.
words: a person in a white coat
The person who helps sick people.
A time you agree for a visit.
I have an appointment at ten.
a big building with a cross
The big place for sick people.
The hospital is outside the city.
To stay until it is your turn.
What you take when you are sick.
a red spot on an arm
question: Is it easy to see a doctor in your city? Why?
model: For me, it is difficult because the doctor is very busy.
choices: a doctor near home or a big hospital
a morning appointment or an evening appointment
call first or go in person
pref_example: I prefer a morning appointment because I work in the evening.

roleplay.title: book an appointment
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at a clinic. Student B calls to book a visit.

future.chunks: Next week, I will… / Tomorrow, I want to…
future.prompts: When will you go to the doctor next? What do you want to ask about?
future.model: Next week I will go to the pharmacy and then to the doctor.

takeaway: One word + one appointment you need this month.
weaker: write the days and times on the board so B only has to choose.
stronger: Tuesday is full, so A offers Thursday afternoon and B must check their calendar.

title: Travel Mindset & Cultural Curiosity
lead: Travel gives beginners a reason to ask questions. Card 4 is a hotel desk, where every sentence is short and useful.
warmup: Show one travel photo on your phone. Say where it is.
say: I have a reservation. / My name is Ana Silva.
words: To go to another city or country.
The paper you buy to travel.
My ticket is in my bag.
A building where you sleep on a trip.
The hotel is near the station.
I have a map on my phone.
I take a photo of the street.
A big town with many people.
question: Do you like travel? Why?
model: For me, travel is good because I see new food and new streets.
choices: plan everything or no plan
a hotel or a flat
a city or the sea
pref_example: I prefer a flat because I can cook.

roleplay.title: check in at a hotel
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at a hotel. Student B has a reservation.

future.chunks: Next year, I want to travel to… / In August, I will…
future.prompts: Where do you want to travel next year? What will you do there?
future.model: Next year I want to travel to Italy and eat in small restaurants.

takeaway: One word + one place you want to see.
weaker: give B a reservation card with name, room and dates written on it.
stronger: the room is not ready, so B has to ask for a place to leave the bags.

title: Social Plans & Boundaries
lead: Saying no politely is the hardest A0 skill and the most useful. This session practises it until it is easy.
warmup: Say one thing you will do this weekend. One sentence.
say: Do you want to come? / Sorry, I am busy.
words: What you will do and when.
A person you like and know well.
The place where you watch films.
question: Is it easy to say no to friends? Why?
model: For me, it is difficult because I don't want to be rude.
choices: say yes always or say no sometimes
plan early or plan at the last minute
a small group or a big group
pref_example: I prefer a small group because I can talk to everybody.

roleplay.title: invite and say no politely
roleplay.scenario: Student A invites Student B out. B is busy and suggests another day.
frames: Do you want to come on Saturday?
Yes, Sunday is good. What time?

future.chunks: Next weekend, I want to… / On Sunday, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to do next weekend? Who will you invite?
future.model: Next weekend I want to have dinner with two friends.

takeaway: One word + one plan you will make this week.
weaker: give B the phrase "Sorry, I am busy" on a card and let them read it.
stronger: B is busy on Saturday and Sunday, so they must suggest a third option.

title: Navigation & Independence
lead: Left, right, straight, near, far: five words that turn a lost beginner into a person who can ask. Card 4 is a small map and a stranger.
warmup: Point left. Point right. Say the words. Your partner does the same.
say: Go left, then right. / It is near the park.
words: The place where a bus stops.
question: Do you use a map on your phone? Why?
model: For me, the map is good because I am often lost.
choices: ask a person or use your phone
walk or take a taxi
go out in the day or at night
pref_example: I prefer to ask a person because it is faster.

roleplay.title: find the pharmacy
roleplay.scenario: Student B is lost. Student A lives in the area and gives directions.
frames: Excuse me, I am lost. Where is the pharmacy?

future.chunks: Next week, I want to go to… / Tomorrow, I will walk to…
future.prompts: Where do you want to go next week? Will you walk or take the bus?
future.model: Next week I want to go to the new market, and I will walk there.

takeaway: One direction word + one place you will go next week.
weaker: draw three streets on paper and let A point while speaking.
stronger: A gives a longer route with four steps, and B repeats it back.

title: Learning Styles & Education Memories
lead: The club itself is the topic: how do you learn, and what helps? Card 4 is a short conversation about an English course.
warmup: Say one word you learned in English this month.
say: I learn English at the club. / It is difficult but good.
words: The person who helps you learn.
I read one book a month.
I learn ten words a week.
a flag and a letter A
Work you do at home for a class.
I do homework on the bus.
To keep something in your mind.
I remember new words with photos.
question: How do you learn best?
model: For me, I learn best with music because I remember the words.
choices: read a book or listen to audio
learn alone or learn in a class
study in the morning or study at night
pref_example: I prefer a class because I can speak with people.

roleplay.title: ask about an English course
roleplay.scenario: Student A works at a language school. Student B wants a course.
frames: We have a class on Monday.
How many people are in the class?

future.chunks: Next year, I want to… / This month, I will…
future.prompts: What do you want to do in English next year? What will you practise this month?
future.model: Next year I want to speak English at work.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will practise this week.
weaker: put the three course times on the board and let B choose.
stronger: the Monday class is full, so A offers a cheaper online class and B must compare.

title: Tech Dependence & Digital Habits
lead: Everyone in the room has a phone, which makes this the easiest session to make concrete. Card 4 is asking for help with it.
warmup: Look at your phone. How many hours yesterday? Say the number.
say: I use my phone a lot. / My phone is off.
words: The glass front of a phone.
I look at the screen too much.
To put electricity in a phone.
I charge my phone at night.
The phone is quiet at night.
question: How many hours do you use your phone? Is it too much?
model: For me, four hours is too much because I sleep late.
choices: phone at dinner or no phone at dinner
phone in the morning or a walk in the morning
send a message or make a call
pref_example: I prefer a call because messages are slow.

roleplay.title: ask for help with a phone
roleplay.scenario: Student B has a problem with a phone. Student A helps.

future.chunks: Tonight, I will… / Next week, I want to…
future.prompts: What time will you turn off your phone tonight? What do you want to do without your phone?
future.model: Tonight I will turn off my phone at ten.

takeaway: One word + one thing you will do without your phone.
weaker: act the problem with the phone in hand, so the words come from the action.
stronger: the phone needs a new battery, so A explains two options and B chooses.

title: Life Reflections & Future Hopes
lead: The last session of the course, so the language looks backwards and forwards: what was good this year, and what comes next.
warmup: Say one good thing about this year. One word is enough.
say: This year was good. / Next year I want to change my job.
words: The work you do for money.
I want to learn to drive.
What you will do and when.
My hope is a quiet flat.
question: What was good this year?
model: For me, this year was good because I met new people.
choices: the same life or a new life
stay in this city or move
learn something now or learn later
pref_example: I prefer to learn now because I have time.

roleplay.title: tell a friend your plan
roleplay.scenario: Two friends talk about next year. A asks questions, B answers.
frames: What do you want to do next year?

future.chunks: Next year, I will… / In five years, I want to…
future.prompts: What will you do next year? Where do you want to be in five years?
future.model: Next year I will start an English course, and in five years I want to work in another country.

takeaway: One word from the course + one thing you will do next year.
weaker: let B answer with one word plus "because" and one noun.
stronger: A has to give one piece of advice — "You can start with a small course."
